source.extractionNote: One of four independent components on the Chip page, each with its own board and its own metadata frame; this spec covers Status Chip only. All 10 variants (status 5 × Rounded 2, complete) extracted and diffed against the default. A single frame with one text child; no instances, no subcomponents.

summary: Shows a read-only state or attribute of an item, such as its progress or availability, so it can be scanned at a glance. It is not interactive and carries no states of its own. Use a filter or assist chip when someone needs to act on it.

label.intent: The state being reported, in a word or two. The chip carries no icon, so the word does all the work and an abbreviation that only makes sense in context will not survive being scanned.

intent.default: No particular standing, for an attribute that is a plain fact rather than good or bad news. Its background is currently an interactive hover token rather than a neutral surface, so it can read as something pressable.
intent.success: A finished or healthy state. The label still has to name what succeeded, because the colour does not.
intent.warning: Something needs attention but has not failed.
intent.negative: A failed or blocking state. Reserve it for something that has to be dealt with, or it stops reading as urgent.
intent.info: Neutral supporting information, where the other four would overstate it.

intent.true: Match the contour of the surface the chip sits on. This chip takes a gentler corner than the other three chip types, so a row that mixes them will not line up.
intent.false: The square-cornered pairing, for surfaces built from sharp controls.

anatomy.role: The component frame. A horizontal auto-layout hugging the label at a fixed height.
anatomy.note: The gap separates nothing: the label is the only child.

anatomy.role: The status signal itself. It is the frame's own fill rather than a separate layer, which is why there is nothing to restyle independently.
The status word. The only content, and the only part that names the state.

variants._note: Complete grid (10 of 10). Only the fill and the radius change; label colour, padding, gap and height are identical everywhere.

tokens._note: All 13 token names resolve in tokens/base. interactive/neutral/border/default and stroke/base are bound on a stroke that renders at zero width; drop both if the border is removed (see issues).

states.whatChanges: The set declares no hover, focus, pressed or disabled axis. A status chip is a label, not a control.
The only things that change across the ten variants are the background token and the corner radius. The label colour stays at interactive/neutral/foreground/default for all five statuses.

behavior.description: Figma stores no timing and nothing transitions. A status chip is replaced when the underlying state changes rather than animated into a new one.
There is no state axis and no nested control. If the chip has to be clicked, it is the wrong component.

content.description: Plain text set per instance, defaulting to Label. The only content the chip takes.
There is no icon slot. Status is carried by background colour and the word alone, which is why the word has to be explicit.

do: Keep the label to the state itself, such as Shipped or Overdue. The colour supports the word, it does not replace it.
Use one status chip per item. A row of them turns a scannable attribute into a puzzle.
dont: Don't make a status chip clickable. It has no states, so it will not respond to hover or focus.
Don't use status=default for a real status. Its background is an interactive hover token, so it reads as a control rather than a label.

accessibility: Status is carried by background colour and the label. The label has to name the state in words, because the colour is not available to everyone.
The label colour is the same token for all five statuses, so contrast varies with the background. Check interactive/neutral/foreground/default against each feedback background.
The chip is not focusable and carries no role. If a screen reader should announce the status, it has to be associated with the item it describes.
The label uses body/xsmall at 12px, the smallest text across the four chip types. Avoid reducing it further.
status=default renders on an interactive hover background, which can read as a control that can be pressed.

layoutTheming.description: 24 tall across all ten variants, the shortest of the four chip types. Width hugs the label.
space/xs top and bottom, space/sm left and right, with a space/xs gap that currently separates nothing because the label is the only child.
radius/element-sm when true and radius/none when false. The other three chip types use radius/pill in the same place.
feedback/success, warning, error and info backgrounds for those four values. status=default uses interactive/neutral/background/hover, an interactive token rather than a surface.
A stroke bound to interactive/neutral/border/default sits on all ten variants at zero weight, so it never renders. Give it a weight or remove it.
body/xsmall at 12 over a 16px line, in interactive/neutral/foreground/default on every status.

visualReference.policy: No images are stored; every node deep-links into Figma so a shot can be pulled on demand and is never stale.

issues.detail: Status Chip does the same job as Status Label (Badges page, set 6403:297): a read-only, non-interactive state word with five standings and the same four feedback/*/background/subtle fills (status Label: neutral/info/positive/warning/negative; this chip: default/info/success/warning/negative). Status Label is the richer one (per-status border, optional dot or icon, body/small text, radius/pill, a feedback/neutral fill for neutral). Both metadata frames describe the same intent ('Shows a read-only state…' vs 'Reports a read-only state…'). Decide which survives before building both; if both stay, share one status→token map.

status=default fills with interactive/neutral/background/hover, an interactive token, so it reads as pressable (the metadata flags this itself). Status Label uses feedback/neutral/background/subtle for the same role; that is the likely fix.
A stroke bound to interactive/neutral/border/default at stroke/base sits on all ten variants and never renders: stroke/base resolves to 0px (primitives scale/0). Omit the border in code.
stroke/base's description says '= 1px' but it resolves to 0px.
One label colour (interactive/neutral/foreground/default) on five backgrounds; contrast per status is unverified here. Check in both palette modes.

Gap space/xs is set but separates nothing (single child). Root hugs vertically; the 24px height is padding plus the body/xsmall line, not a fixed size, so it scales with the size and typography modes.

Rounded uses radius/element-sm here and radius/pill on the other three chips, and the label is body/xsmall (Regular) where the others use a Medium label style. A mixed row will not line up (metadata says so too).
No interaction states by design; no motion. Name difference to reconcile if merged with Status Label: success↔positive, default↔neutral.
